title: the system device publishes a launch tool that answers the launch path's OS questions
intention: cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch, a tool the system device publishes, answers every OS question the launch path asks: venv_bin_dir, box_addresses, port_listening, runs_shell_scripts, stream_is_console, service_spawn, scoped_exec and elevation. Each action returns {ok, how, detail}, and 'not on this box' is a stated answer.
why: Measured 2026-11-22: cairn/devices/cc/superclaude answers eight OS questions in bash (uname at :10 and :386, hostname -I at :19, sudo at :326-360, systemd-run units at :620-760, ss -tlnH at :717, systemd-run --scope at :860-880). A Python superclaude (c3cd232ba0cf child 3) must ask them somewhere, and RULE 1 plus Akien 2026-11-21 ('hostname should come from the system device') put every OS answer in the system device.
traces_to: RULE 1; outline 5.4.3.8 (Windows needs no bash); Law 1 (one answer per OS question).
how: One module, launch.py, beside host/host.py, with a charter marked published_by_device. On Linux each answer reproduces the bash: venv_bin_dir picks Scripts or bin through host.os_id(); box_addresses reads hostname -I; port_listening reads the kernel's listening table (/proc/net/tcp and tcp6, state 0A; netstat on nt), never dialing, since sole_path forbids this tool a module that can dial; stream_is_console is isatty; runs_shell_scripts is os_id() != 'windows'; service_spawn runs systemd-run --user --unit with HOME/PATH setenv and append logs, reset-failed and retries once on 'already loaded', returns held when the unit is active, and falls back to setsid (start_new_session) when systemd-run is absent; on nt it spawns with windowless_spawn.detached_kwargs. scoped_exec execs under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryHigh/Max/SwapMax when a scope can start, else a plain exec, and states which. elevation reports passwordless, password-held (CAIRN_SUDO_PW checks with sudo -S -k over stdin) or none; on nt it reports whether the token is elevated (shell32 IsUserAnAdmin).

clauses.claim: on Linux, venv_bin_dir, box_addresses, port_listening (a port the proof binds vs one it does not), stream_is_console (a pty vs a pipe) and runs_shell_scripts return what the bash computes on this box for the same input
service_spawn starts a uniquely named transient user unit, and a second call while it runs returns held and starts nothing
scoped_exec runs a child whose own cgroup memory.max equals the MemoryMax passed (UNMEASURED off a box with systemd --user)
every result names how it was answered (systemd, setsid, detached, scope, plain, not-on-this-box), and none is empty

decisions.text: D1: a new published tool beside host, not an extension of host: host answers 'which box' and stays pure; launch spawns and execs. Its whole text is D4 (launch.py) and D5 (the charter); write each exactly as given.

D2: launch.py imports detached_kwargs and windowless_kwargs from cairn.tools.windowless_spawn.windowless_spawn (cairn/tools/windowless_spawn/windowless_spawn.py:24 and :34; each takes an optional os_name and returns a dict of Popen keyword arguments). Every subprocess call in launch.py passes **windowless_kwargs(); the nt branch of service_spawn passes **detached_kwargs() instead, so the service outlives the caller with no console window. The POSIX setsid fallback passes start_new_session=True plus **windowless_kwargs() (detached_kwargs on POSIX also sets start_new_session, so the two never both appear).

D3: the red-first proof is already written and sealed red on main (commit b3c17da82) at cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch/proofs/test_the_launch_tool_answers_the_launch_paths_os_questions.py; the build does not edit it. It imports the tool inside each tooth, keys PROVES to clauses 1-4, names its unit cairn-launch-proof-<pid>-<time> and its scope cairn-launch-proof-scope-<pid>, stops and reset-fails the unit at teardown, and prints UNMEASURED for a tooth this box cannot run. The build's only act on it is the green reseal: bin/cairn test --seal cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch/proofs/test_the_launch_tool_answers_the_launch_paths_os_questions.py, which writes the validation beside it.

D5: write cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/launch/intention+why.json exactly so, through the artifact door (cairn artifact write --verb cast), which takes only canonical JSON, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus a newline (sha256 8564dc3169a1e85960382c1fd997420d1d072eabbef0196d72d3b94902fccc8d), modeled on the host charter:
